- If sentiment is consistently bearish (avg < 0.5) and model forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If recent price spike is followed by model forecast continuing upward, apply downward correction to prevent overshoot.
- When official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model should not overcorrect downward — allow slight mean reversion but avoid deep dips.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp decline, reduce forecast slope or introduce early downward bias.
- For high event count with net supply negative, model should not overestimate downward trend — adjust for event-induced volatility, not just supply.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend — apply smoothing or lagged adjustment.
- When sentiment is bullish but true outcome declines, model should not ignore recent events — adjust downward bias based on event count and supply net.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 10-day moving average, apply mean reversion correction to avoid overconfidence in trend.
